title: Ordinary and completed tensor agree on integral constructible complexes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $W$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and completed coefficient sheaf $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $M\otimes^L_BN$ be the ordinary ambient derived tensor product, computed by the total tensor of flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and let $M\widehat\otimes^L_RN$ be the completed tensor product [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Then $M\otimes^L_BN$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], and the canonical comparison
$$
\chi_{M,N}:M\otimes^L_BN\longrightarrow M\widehat\otimes^L_RN
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $M,N$. Here $\chi$ is the canonical map from the ordinary tensor complex to the product mapping-fiber complex of its reduction tower: on flat-term K-flat representatives $P\to M$, $Q\to N$ its level-$n$ map is the coefficient quotient map
$$
\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_BQ)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Res}_n\operatorname{Tot}\bigl((P\otimes_B(A_n)_W)\otimes_{(A_n)_W}(Q\otimes_B(A_n)_W)\bigr),
$$
with the strict quotient transitions, and the completed tensor on the right is the derived limit of this tower.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5, pp. 49–50 (the ordinary derived tensor of constructible complexes is already complete), with Definition 6.5.1 and Lemmas 6.5.3–6.5.4, p. 49; Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12(4), pp. 22–23 (completed tensor and canonical reduction-tower completion). Specialization R=O_E; its residue ring is a field, so the constructibility convention agrees with def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed.

proof.text: For any qcqs scheme $T$ in the argument, write $C_T(H)=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(H\otimes^L_{B_T}(A_n)_T)$ and $\eta_H:H\to C_T(H)$ for the functorial completion and its quotient-map unit. The constant/completed equivalence identifies this completion, including its unit, with Koszul completion; the ringed Koszul reflector says its values are locally complete and that $\eta_H$ is invertible exactly on such objects. If $H$ is complete in the Roos-triangle sense of def-weil-derived-complete, it is isomorphic to $C_T(H)$: both are fibers of the same $1-s$ on the same derived product. Thus $H$ is locally complete and its particular canonical map $\eta_H$ is invertible. Conversely an invertible $\eta_H$ gives the required Roos triangle. This explicitly handles the definition's warning that an arbitrary triangulated lift of the quotient maps is not a specified completion unit.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion, with ringed Koszul reflector and functorial strict-tower model; Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12(4)

proof.text: Completion commutes with the restrictions used below. For a weakly etale object $V\to T$, identify its site with the slice by the localization theorem. Slice restriction is exact and preserves products and constant sheaves by the formula $F|_V(U\to V)=F(U)$: local lifts of sections are tested on the same covering families. For a constructible closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with quasi-compact open complement, the closed-pullback limits theorem says $i^*$ is exact and preserves all limits. Consequently $i^*B_T=B_Z$, and similarly on slices. Countable products of module sheaves are exact on each of these pro-etale sites, so termwise products represent derived products. In both cases apply the exact, product-preserving restriction termwise to the product mapping fiber defining $C_T$; exactness and product preservation identify it with $C_V$ or $C_Z$. Derived monoidality identifies the restricted finite reductions, and these identifications carry $h\mapsto h\otimes1$ and the quotient transitions to the corresponding maps on the restricted site. Thus restrictions commute with $\eta$, not merely with its source and target. They preserve completeness by step 1.

source.place: Tag 09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply (closed pullback preserves limits); Tag 0990 and localized sites; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2)

proof.text: The finitely many nonzero residue cohomology sheaves of $M,N$ admit finite locally closed constructible partitions by the constructibility definitions. Apply lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement to these partitions. Its factorizations have quasi-compact open complements, and its finite open–closed splitting tree has qcqs leaves, each nonempty leaf $T$ mapping scheme-theoretically through one stratum of each partition; on an empty leaf every restricted sheaf is zero, so the conditions below hold trivially. Step 2 therefore applies at every branch: the restricted $M,N$ remain canonically complete and their residue cohomology on $T$ is bounded locally constant finite-dimensional over the residue field. The residue field is a field by the coefficient datum.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, constructible residue stratification and restriction

proof.text: For each leaf $T$, take the affine weakly contractible cover $V\to T$ of lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qc-affine-contractible-cover. The slice-site equivalence of lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization also makes $V$ weakly contractible in its own site: a covering of $V$ there is a covering in $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, so its representable epimorphism splits, and the same lifting argument splits local lifts of any sheaf epimorphism over $V$. By step 2 and exact monoidal restriction, $M|_V,N|_V$ remain complete and their residue cohomology retains the hypotheses of lem-fix-constructible-flat-cohomology-tor-bound. Apply that lemma to each: it supplies precisely the interval bound for arbitrary module sheaves on every slice required by lem-fix-residue-lisse-projective-models. The latter gives finite disjoint open covers with bounded finite-projective $B$-models. Intersect the two finite covers; pullback retains each inclusion–retraction diagram, so both models exist on a common cover.

source.place: Tags 09C3 and 0990, local projective models on affine weakly contractible objects

proof.text: On each chart the coefficient unit $B$ is canonically complete. Indeed its reduction is $(A_n)$ in degree zero, with the usual surjective transitions on sections by the constant-module section theorem. The map $1-s$ on their product is surjective on every section set: given $(y_n)$ choose $x_1$ and recursively lift $x_n-y_n$ to $x_{n+1}$. Its kernel is $\varprojlim_n(A_n)=B$. Exact countable products and the Roos model therefore identify $\eta_B:B\to C(B)$ with an isomorphism. For exactness of the entire completion functor, consider on complexes the strict tower $F(P)_n=P\otimes_B(A_n)$ with its quotient transitions. This additive construction commutes with shifts and mapping cones (all cone sums are finite), and composing its image in the strict-tower derived category with $R\lim$ is exact by the strict-tower theorem. Every complex has a K-flat replacement; a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes induces a quasi-isomorphism at each reduction by derived change of rings, hence in the strict-tower category because its kernels and cohomology are levelwise. The resolving-class theorem therefore gives an exact functor $C$ on $D(B)$, computed by these same K-flat towers. It is additive, so $\eta$ is invertible on every direct summand of a finite sum of $B$ (restrict its inverse along the summand inclusions and projections). It is then invertible on a bounded complex of such terms: start with a single term, and use successive finite brutal-truncation cone triangles and the long exact cohomology sequences to pass from two invertible components of a morphism of triangles to the third.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion; Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, and the sectionwise Roos calculation; finite-complex dévissage

proof.text: Tensor the two bounded projective sheaf models on a common chart. Their total tensor is bounded; a tensor of two summands of $B^r$ and $B^s$ is a summand of $B^{rs}$ by tensoring the inclusion and retraction maps. Its terms are finite sums of such summands. These terms are flat since the free-unit tensor functor is a finite sum of identity functors and exactness passes to direct summands. A bounded complex of flat sheaves is K-flat: tensor an acyclic complex with each flat term, then build the bounded tensor total by the finite stupid filtration, whose successive quotients are those acyclic termwise tensors. Thus this total computes the ordinary derived tensor of the restricted $M,N$. Step 5 makes its canonical completion map invertible.

source.place: Tag 09C3 finite-projective models; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.5.5, finite-projective dévissage; explicit bounded-flat argument

proof.text: Put $H=M\otimes^L_BN$. Steps 2 and 6 show that the restriction of the actual map $\eta_H$ to each chart over every piece $T$ is invertible. Hence its cone restricts to zero on $T$: a complex of sheaves whose cohomology vanishes on a covering is acyclic, since a section of a sheaf is zero when its restrictions to a covering vanish. Now reverse the finite open–closed splitting tree of step 3. At any split, if a complex has zero restrictions to the open and closed children, apply the exact sequence $0\to j_!j^*F\to F\to i_*i^*F\to0$ to each cohomology sheaf $F$; exactness of the two inverse images makes both end terms zero, hence $F=0$. Inducting up the tree shows that the cone of $\eta_H$ is zero on $W$, so $\eta_H$ is an isomorphism. By step 1, $H$ is derived complete in the Roos-triangle sense of def-weil-derived-complete.

source.place: Tag 09BM, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact, and the open–closed exact sequence; Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 6.5.5 and 6.5.8

proof.text:
Finally identify $C_W(H)$ with the tensor operation in the statement. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $P\to M$, $Q\to N$; these exist by the resolution theorem. Derived monoidality for the identity of the topos equipped with $B\to(A_n)_W$ gives
$$H\otimes^L_B(A_n)_W\simeq (M\otimes^L_B(A_n)_W)\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(N\otimes^L_B(A_n)_W).$$
On the chosen representatives this is the balancing isomorphism
$$((p\otimes q)\otimes a)\longmapsto (p\otimes a)\otimes(q\otimes1).$$
Its inverse multiplies the two scalar factors. These maps preserve degree and commute with the tensor differentials, as all scalars have degree zero. They commute with quotient transitions by the identity $\rho_n(ab)=\rho_n(a)\rho_n(b)$, and send the quotient map to the map displayed in the item. The changed-ring representatives are K-flat, so they compute all finite-level derived tensors. Applying the functorial product mapping fiber identifies $C_W(H)$ with $M\widehat\otimes_R^LN$ and $\eta_H$ with exactly $\chi_{M,N}$, which is therefore invertible by step 7. All balancing and quotient maps commute with maps in $P,Q$; the tensor descent theorem extends this equality uniquely to the derived categories. Together with functoriality of the strict-tower derived limit, this proves naturality in both variables.
